name: everwrite
topic: the signs of AI-generated prose and how to write without them: pattern catalogues, humanizer skills, checkers, what current models still overuse

volatile_claims.claim: Em dashes are a historical tell: Wikipedia moved the sign to Historical indicators 2026-10-07; Opus 5.5 uses 0.015 per 1,000 words (Graphite, Oct 2026); only older Claude models overuse them
blader/humanizer (3.1.0) is the most-starred prose humanizer skill and ships no checker; maintained checkers exist outside the skills (tbhb/vale-ai-tells, berelevant-ai/slopless)
Wikipedia eras: GPT-5 words (emphasizing, enhance, highlighting, showcasing) mid-2025 to mid-2026; GPT-6 era list added Oct 2026 by a temporary account (dependable, quietly, matters, steady...)
Claude text is watermarked (SynthID-Text style, no added characters) for models from 2026-08-02; older models by December 2026; detection is a private preview
OpenAI textGrain watermarks ChatGPT and Codex text for EU users (rollout from 2026-10-05; API opt-in elsewhere); detection limited to approved researchers
No public checker exists for deployed text watermarks; SynthID Detector is public since 2026-10-07 for images, video and audio only

events.label: EU AI Act Art. 50(2) grace period ends; Anthropic's retrofit target for older models; OpenAI text marking likely
